recipes.name: The Best Bean and Ham Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 (20 ounce) package 15-bean soup mix (seasoning packet not used)
1 (12 fluid ounce) can low-sodium vegetable juice
1 teaspoon kosher salt, or to taste

steps.text: Place beans into a large container and cover with several inches of cool water; let soak, 8 hours to overnight.
Drain beans and transfer to a large pot. Fill with enough water to cover by about 1 inch; bring to a boil over medium heat. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 30 minutes. Drain.

Add ham, ham bone, carrots, celery, onion, and undrained diced tomatoes to the pot. Stir in vegetable broth, vegetable juice, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, Dijon, chili powder, parsley, pepper, and bay leaves. Pour in enough chicken broth to cover ingredients and simmer over low heat, stirring occasionally and adding more chicken broth as needed, for about 8 hours.
Remove and discard ham bone and season soup with salt. Continue to simmer for 1 to 2 hours. Remove bay leaves before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: The Best Bean and Ham Soup
raw_recipe.description: If you like 7-bean soup, you'll love this version made with a dried 15-bean mix, ham, and vegetables that slowly simmers all day on your stove.

video.description: This video shows you how to make a hearty, flavorful white bean and ham soup. Easy and hands off, this top-rated soup is a great way to get the most from your Easter or Christmas ham. It gets big flavor from long-simmering with the ham bone. It really feeds a crowd—and the leftovers might be even better.

review.reviewBody: I wrote this recipe and the directions printed are not as I wrote them. Here they are: Remove and discard seasoning packet, if any, from beans. Place beans in large stockpot. Cover with water to 2 inches over beans and soak overnight. Drain the soaking water from the beans. Cover beans with fresh water and bring to boil. Reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, 30 minutes. Drain again, discarding water. Remove all visible fat from ham bone. Combine beans, ham bone, ham, onion, celery, carrots, tomatoes, V8, Worcestershire, mustard, chili powder, bay leaves, pepper, parsley, lemon juice, and vegetable stock in stockpot. Add chicken stock to cover beans. Bring to boil. Reduce heat, and simmer, stirring occasionally, for about 8 hours. Add remaining chicken stock to the pot throughout the day as needed to keep liquid level up. After about 8 hours, remove the ham bone, and add salt as needed. Continue simmering another 2 hours, or until beans are tender. Remove bay leaves before serving.

In the 16 yrs, I've been a mom & housewife I have stayed away from bean soup because I had a horrible experience as a kid with it ... let's say it wasn't one of mom's greatest recipes and sadly she made it all too often!
But this recipe ... Oh My ... DELISH! I will make bean soup again for sure. I was skeptic as to the igredients it called for and reviewed a few other recipes on this site as well, I followed this recipe to the letter adding some brown sugar as well and I followed suggestions from other users to add the baking soda. I used more ham then what the recipe called for only because of the memories of bean soup as a kid. Let's just say that my own children will have terrific memories of bean soup when they get older and will probably want this recipe from me when they get older. :O) Thanks so much for sharing this!!

Very nice recipe and very easy. Two changes I made. I did not use stock, I used water and a ham hock instead of ham. The soup was still very flavorful and had less fat and sodium using water instead of stock. I also quick soak the beans by boiling them for 3 minutes and then soaking them in the hot water for 1 hour.

Absolutely Fabulous! My modifications: I made a broth in my Instapot with the ham bone leftover from Christmas dinner. I tossed in odds and ends celery, onion, 5 cloves of garlic, sweet potato peels. I drained the broth into a pot on the stove, that I had browned the celery and onions and carrots. In my haste, I DID NOT presoak the bag of black beans. As I reread the recipe, I thought I really screwed up. But as it turns out, I just had to simmer for 7 hours on the stove. I didn't have enough ham, so I cut up a precooked turkey breast and added it to the soup while it simmered.
My changes in sum: Used ham bone broth instead of vegetable broth, added turkey in addition to the bits of ham and did not rinse or soak the beans. 
I also garnished with fresh cilantro and fresh lime juice.
Best bean soup I have ever had!

I’ve made this soup many times, and my kids and I love it. Switched it up a little today and wanted to share. I wanted to use up some of my frozen turkey from thanksgiving. I used two smoked turkey wings and simmered them for an few hours. Took them out and pulled the meat off and put it back in the soup. Added about 2 cups of the leftover turkey. Simmered a few more hours and added chopped Swiss chard. It was AMAZING! Love the original, but I think I like the turkey and Swiss chard addition even more. Great any way you make it!

My revisions: I soaked beans overnight, rinsed and drained and then added water to cover beans.....but did not cook for 30 minutes and then discard that cooking water as the recipe states. I just added all the broths to the beans covered in water. Used all low sodium broths. I used a left over from Christmas meaty ham bone, 2 whole carrots, 5 whole cloves of garlic, 2 whole stalks of celery and 1 large onion cut in quarters. After 5 hours of cooking; I fished out the large ham bone and the whole carrots, celery, and onion. I cut off the meat that hadn’t fallen off the bone and put that back in the pot, then added the can of diced tomatoes, chopped carrots, onions, celery the last 45 minutes of cooking. The last 15 minutes of cooking added a couple handfuls of fresh baby spinach and the juice from a half of fresh lemon. I’ve taught cooking for 22 years and I am so impressed with this recipe’s seasoning—-just fabulous!

Turned out awesome.
Made it in a 6 qt INSTANT POT. 
Modifications as follows:
Sautee veggies first
Mix in all condiments and spices.
Add diced tomatoes and rinsed beans (don't soak)
Add 50oz can chicken stock and low sodium V8
Add ham bone, plus cubed chunks
Skip veggie stock and salt. 
Could do 50/50 on chicken/veggie stock, to reduce salt.
45 minutes manual high pressure
Natural pressure release recommended
(I had to finally manual release the pressure after 55min of waiting.)

I make this recipe after each time I make a bone-in ham. It is an incredible flavorful and homey family favorite. The only change I make is not soaking the beans. I cook the beans for 30 minutes with the addition of 1/4 tsp baking soda. I then rinse the beans and add back into the pot. I then add all the ingredients as instructed with the addition of another 1/4 tsp baking soda. The beans cook much faster and are creamy, saving hours of time.

This is a great base for ham and bean soup and can be easily changed to your taste. To reduce liquid, I just used chicken broth and no vegetable juice/vegetable broth. Based on another review, I subbed Rotel instead on diced tomatoes. I also subbed 1tsp liquid smoke instead of worcestershire sauce. I used 1tsp dry mustard rather than Dijon. I added some cayenne pepper and potatoes. Since I don't like to soak beans due to time, I used 4 cans of white beans and 1/2 can of refried beans to thicken it. Also, I forgot the lemon juice at the end but the flavor was great so we ate it the way it was. Everyone loved it and it was a great way to use up leftover Easter ham. Thanks!

This was yummy! I did the fast soak of the beans - boiled for 3 minutes, then left in the hot water for 3 hours. I sauteed the onions and celery in 2 T butter and 2T olive oil. I made this in the InstantPot. When I added the beans, veggies, ham and ham bone - it wouldn't all fit. I actually had about 5 cups of cubed ham, so I just didn't use the ham bone. I used about 1 1/2 cups chicken broth, a can of fire roasted diced tomatoes, the bottle of vegetable juice. At this point everything in the InstantPot was covered in liquid, so I did not add any vegetable broth or more chicken broth. It turned out great, with plenty of liquid in the soup. I served it with some Everything Sourdough Bread. So good! Thank you!

Awesome! It's on my keeper list. Could not find any any ham bones so used ham hocks instead. The meat manager suggested oxtail, which I had never tasted, but added about 1.5 lbs. it was a very nice additional taste. I took the oxtail bones out after about 6 hrs and shredded and returned any remaining meat to the pot. There is a lot of fat on oxtail so you should trim as much of it as you can see.
This soup is delicious. The only suggestion I have is to go easy on the salt. Depending on the the ham you use it can go either way.

I didn't follow the recipe exactly, but was close replica the way I made it. I always preferred my bean soup with some tomatoes in the base with interesting spices added to the mix. Very happy with the results.
Exactly what I was looking for I like the tomato base so much more than the other versions
I halved the recipe. Used ham and chicken broth. No bone. Did the quick soak method. Only needed to cook about 4 hours
Perfect

As I work, used the suggestions by others to adapt the recipe for using in a slow cooker . Used the hambone/diced ham from the Christmas leftovers. My husband and I really liked it! A keeper recipe for us!
The last time I made this I was told that it was the best soup they had ever eaten, anywhere. The flavors in this soup are amazing.
Just made this X2 per recipe. Best soup I've made. Will freeze half and expect it to be even better in the coming months. Thanks!!

Amazing soup!! I modified it a bit. I used great northern beans instead of the bean mix. I didn't use any vegetable broth, I used chicken broth. Also it only took 6 hours to cook. Worth the effort!!!!!!
